cards.headline: Unpaid wages: Director behind firms linked to case back in S’pore; man is assisting MOM probe
bullets: The director of three firms accused of not paying migrant workers is back in Singapore and helping with the probe.
Over 300 migrant workers claimed they had not been paid wages for more than two months.
The Ministry of Manpower is helping affected workers find new jobs.
Some workers have moved out of their dorms to a new centre while seeking new employment.

cards.headline: Man who went missing on June 23 found dead in waters off Coney Island; no foul play suspected
bullets: A 50-year-old man reported missing on June 23 was found dead off Coney Island on June 24.
Police had appealed for information on his whereabouts after he was last seen in Punggol.
His body was retrieved from the waters near Coney Island.
Police do not suspect foul play at this time.

cards.headline: SPF trials new canine-mounted camera system to improve search operations
bullets: Police dogs are now testing cameras on their harnesses for search operations.
The cameras give officers a dog's-eye view of areas before they enter.
This helps officers see threats and dangers in dark or tight spaces.
The system also has audio to talk to people during searches.

cards.headline: Dads get postpartum depression too
bullets: About 10 per cent of dads can get depression or anxiety after their child is born.
Fathers might show anger or irritation when they are feeling down.
Some dads hide their struggles with drugs, alcohol, or gambling.
New fathers can feel overwhelmed by changes in routine and identity.

cards.headline: Elderly motorcyclist dies in hospital after accident on TPE; car driver arrested
bullets: An 80-year-old motorcyclist died in hospital after a crash on the TPE.
Police arrested a 40-year-old car driver for causing death by careless driving.
The accident happened on the TPE towards the SLE on June 27.
Investigations into the fatal crash are still ongoing.

cards.headline: Employer of hundreds of unpaid migrant workers back in Singapore: Manpower Ministry
bullets: The employer of over 400 unpaid migrant workers is back in Singapore and helping with investigations.
His passport has been taken away as part of the probe.
The Ministry of Manpower is taking the unpaid wages issue very seriously.
Hundreds of workers have been offered new jobs and support.

cards.headline: Low Thia Khiang says he will support Pritam Singh ahead of special cadres conference
bullets: Low Thia Khiang said he supports Pritam Singh ahead of a Workers' Party meeting.
The party is holding a special conference about Pritam Singh's conviction.
Pritam Singh was convicted of lying to a parliamentary committee.
The Workers' Party will also elect its leaders at the conference.

cards.headline: Singapore police trialling mounted cameras on K-9 unit dogs
bullets: Police dogs are being tested with cameras on their backs.
The cameras give officers a live view of what the dogs see.
This helps police know if someone is dangerous or armed.
The system can also see heat signatures in the dark.
It allows two-way talking through the dog's gear.

cards.headline: Thousands show up at Hong Lim Park for 18th Pink Dot rally
bullets: Thousands gathered at Hong Lim Park for the 18th Pink Dot rally.
The event encourages people to connect with and hear stories from the LGBTQ community.
This is the fourth Pink Dot rally since the repeal of Section 377A.
An MP noted the diversity of support and positivity within the community.
Organisers hope to advance equality and improve daily lives for LGBTQ people.

cards.headline: LVMH and Accor’s Orient Express sets its sights on new tech billionaire class
bullets: Spending on luxury experiences is expected to grow 9-11% this year.
Orient Express is launching a new luxury yacht to attract rich tech bosses.
The venture is a partnership between hotel group Accor and LVMH.
Suites on the new yacht cost from around S$36,000 for a four-day trip.

cards.headline: Tesla Model Y L review: This Tesla defies expectations in one important way
bullets: The Tesla Model Y L costs S$144,264 without COE and has 514 horsepower.
Despite being a six-seater SUV, the Model Y L handles corners well and drives nicely.
It offers a long driving range of 681 km on a single charge.
Build quality issues and a lack of some common features are notable downsides.
The car's handling and efficiency impressed the reviewer, changing their view on larger cars.

cards.headline: Could Ohmyhome face Nasdaq delisting after selling its core unit for US$1? Experts weigh in
bullets: Ohmyhome sold its main property business for just US$1.
The company's shares are trading below Nasdaq's US$1 minimum price requirement.
Ohmyhome is now shifting to become a digital marketing firm.
Experts question if Ohmyhome can remain listed on the Nasdaq.

cards.headline: Real estate firm Ohmyhome’s journey over the past 10 years
bullets: Ohmyhome sold its main property sales business for just US$1.
The company will now focus only on digital marketing.
Ohmyhome listed on the Nasdaq stock market in March 2023.
Its share price has dropped significantly since a peak in May 2023.
The firm recently did a stock split to avoid being delisted.

cards.headline: Bar Kap in the House of Tan Yeok Nee serves up cocktails with Teochew flair
bullets: A new cocktail bar called Bar Kap has opened in the historic House of Tan Yeok Nee.
The bar's drinks are inspired by Teochew heritage and history.
It uses an old technique of ageing drinks in clay pots.
The bar is located in Singapore's last remaining 1800s Teochew mansion.

cards.headline: Shopee deliveryman allegedly fakes wrong delivery to neighbour's unit, takes photo for 'proof', then leaves with parcel
bullets: Shopee refunded a customer and disciplined a rider who allegedly faked a wrong delivery.
The rider took a blurry photo at a neighbour's door before leaving with the parcel.
The customer shared doorbell camera footage showing the deliveryman's actions.
The missing parcel was a S$140 coffee accessory.

cards.headline: Japan 'snow monkey' park to limit visitors over bad tourist behaviour, overcrowding
bullets: Japan's famous monkey park will limit visitors to 2,000 daily starting August 2026.
This change comes after overcrowding and bad tourist behaviour, like trying to feed or bathe with the monkeys.
The park will switch to online ticketing to manage the long queues.
Tourists have also caused issues at other Japanese attractions, leading to similar restrictions.

cards.headline: You Can Complete Fun Quests During The CCL6 Public Preview On 4th July For A Chance To Win FairPrice Vouchers
bullets: Win FairPrice vouchers by completing quests at the new Circle Line stations on July 4th.
The Circle Line will finally be complete on July 12th, 2026.
Preview the new stations for free and enjoy activities on July 4th.
New stations at Keppel, Cantonment, and Prince Edward Road have unique designs.

cards.headline: 8 Best Go-Karting Circuits In JB From $6/Ride, Including Indoor Venues & Electric Kart Options
bullets: Go-karting in Johor starts from S$10.95 for a 8-minute session at KF Kiddy Circuit.
RUD Karting Medini offers a long 874m track with 16 corners and late closing hours.
Permas Go-Kart Club has a 1.4km track and is known for its cheap rates.
X Park Sunway Iskandar features a covered go-kart track and other adventure sports.
Evolt Karting Johor provides an indoor electric go-karting experience with a trackside lounge.

cards.headline: 7 Best Football Academies In Singapore To Nurture Future World Cup Stars In The Making
bullets: Barça Academy Singapore offers free try-outs for kids aged 4 to 17.
Real Madrid Foundation Football School Singapore focuses on values like teamwork and discipline.
Borussia Academy Singapore trains kids with a focus on maximising touches on the ball.
Celtic Soccer Academy Singapore is FAS-accredited and trains kids aged 2 to 12.
